segments.title: Crowds and contemplation at Sanjusangen-do in Kyoto
segments.summary: Large tour groups disperse quickly at Sanjusangen-do, leaving time and space for quiet reflection during the visit.
segments.body: ShipShape trips aim to build an understanding of culture as well as history, alongside the facts and figures. The coaches and crowds at Sanjusangen-do in Kyoto initially suggest a tourist trap, but the experience inside is quiet enough for reflection. Other Japanese temples visited during the trip have also felt peaceful even in busy city districts. Large tour groups disperse quickly, leaving people time to wander through. The visit follows a walk across from the National Museum in Kyoto, near the train station, and reverses an initial expectation that the 600-yen admission would be disappointing. No temple chronology is given; the focus is how a heavily visited religious site can retain a spiritual atmosphere. A personal 'zero or 100 percent' theory developed during the trip suggests that Japan either does not care about something or cares for it completely, with temples in the latter category. At the close, only a few people are still wandering nearby.

evidence.note: He contrasts an initial impression of a tourist trap with the quiet, visitor flow, and contemplative experience preserved inside the temple grounds. At 0:40-0:58 he compares the quiet of other Japanese temples in busy city districts, and at 2:40-2:45 he notes that only a few people are still wandering nearby. The zero-or-100-percent theory at 2:18-2:33 is a personal impression developed during the trip.
